messages:
jess: Submitted a docs PR for Troubleshooting -> Rate limits & timeouts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/512  
jess: Main asks: clarify Retry-After vs X-RateLimit-Reset, add idiomatic Go retry example, document fallback header behavior, and a short migration note for old SDKs that silently trimmed contexts. Can someone skim for accuracy? :wave:
rahul: Will review. Quick note: we should separate short burst 429s from sustained capacity 429s and add concrete ops checks for each. Also call out 413 behavior for over-max-context.
emily: Agreed. For examples, I can add a tiny Go snippet using context.WithTimeout + backoff. That will help Go users who currently copy JS/Python. Proposed: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 12*time.Second)
defer cancel()
backoff := time.Second
for i:=0; i<4; i++ {
  resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, prompt)
  if err == nil { return resp }
  if IsRateLimit(err) {
    // prefer Retry-After header if present
    wait := parseRetryAfter(err)
    if wait == 0 { wait = backoff }
    time.Sleep(wait)
    backoff *= 2
    continue
  }
  return nil, err
}
return nil, fmt.Errorf("retries exhausted")
```
jess: Nice, include comment about respecting Retry-After (seconds) and X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch) and prefer the larger of wait candidates.
rahul: On fallback: public phrasing should be: "When enabled by routing policy, Redwood may transparently route to a compatible model variant under capacity pressure. If routing is disallowed, requests receive 429 with Retry-After." That's safe. Also add note about the response header we set: `x-rw-fallback: true|false` when a fallback was used.
emily: I added a small FAQ entry: "How to detect fallback vs 429?" Answer: check HTTP status (429) and headers: Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Reset; check x-rw-fallback for transparent fallback events.\ess: tiny typo above^^
jess: fixed. Another migration item: older SDKs silently truncated inputs; new behavior returns 413 if token length > model.max_context. Draft text: "If you see 413, run client-side tokenization and windowing. We recommend `truncate` param or streaming windowing library." Add sample token-checker link to Console limits.
rahul: Add a short token-check snippet in JS using our tokenizer util: `const toks = tokenizer.count(input); if (toks > modelMax) { ... }` Also suggest `response_mode=buffered` when apps cannot handle partial outputs after fallback.
emily: For timeouts, include example of AbortController too:
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 10000);
try {
  await client.generate({input, signal: ac.signal});
} catch (e) { if (e.name === 'AbortError') { /* handle */ }}
```
rahul: Ops checklist for docs: 1) Console: check requests_per_minute and allocation usage; 2) Traces: find trace-id header; 3) Look for 429 spikes grouped by route; 4) If Dedicated, verify GPU pool allocation. Add that as bulleted checklist.
jess: Added checklist. Editor note: I left internal Console links as placeholders to avoid premature link breakage; will swap before merging. Also added a tiny curl example showing how to inspect Retry-After: 
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"..."}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# look for 'Retry-After' and 'x-rw-fallback' headers
```
runtime-bot: Reminder: please include a changelog entry under docs/changes if you modify example behavior or add new headers.
emily: One more: doc must explicitly say we sometimes return `Retry-After: 0` for very short burst retry candidates — recommend min backoff 200ms to avoid thundering herd.\jess: Good catch. I'll add that and then request editorial review. Anything else?
rahul: Add test note: docs/tests should include a small unit that asserts header names are mentioned.
jess: Done. Thanks y'all :sparkles:
emily: LGTM :thumbsup: 
runtime-bot: Please wait for runtime sign-off before merging public-facing fallback wording.
